name: CA-35
label: Safe D

key_factors: Incumbent Norma Torres holds a massive fundraising edge ($885K raised, $364K on hand vs. under $10K for Cargile)
District fundamentals favor Democrats (D+6 lean) with a favorable national environment in the baseline
Prediction markets price a Democratic win near 97 percent
No public polling or expert ratings, leaving the margin estimate dependent on fundamentals
model.rationale: Torres combines incumbency, a D+6 district, and an overwhelming money advantage against a challenger with almost no resources, and markets agree the race is not in serious doubt. The absence of polling keeps uncertainty elevated but nowhere near enough to threaten the outcome.
model.watch: Any polling that emerges showing a single-digit race, or a late surge of outside spending on Cargile's behalf, would be the main signal to revisit this forecast.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Norma Torres, the Democratic incumbent, enters the general election as a clear favorite in a district that leans Democratic by six points. She has raised roughly $885,000 and holds about $364,000 on hand, while Republican Mike Cargile has raised under $10,000 with only a few hundred dollars available. No public polls track the race, and no expert raters list it as competitive.

Prediction markets give Torres roughly a 97 percent chance of winning, and the fundamentals point the same way: incumbency, a large money gap, and a favorable district lean. The main source of uncertainty is the absence of polling, which keeps the margin estimate broad. Even with a strong national environment for Republicans, Cargile would need a shift well beyond anything indicated by current evidence to contend.
